transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-27
Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Mateo (Redwood SE), Lina (CSM), Jordan (Apollo), Samir (Apollo CTO), Priya (Lead SRE), Elliot (PM)
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-2026-01-27-apollo-0047

Summary (auto): quick demo of tiered rate fencing, sticky routing, and fallback to cheaper model variants; discussion of PII handling and private deployment options; pilot next steps agreed.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Hey everyone, thanks for taking time today. Quick intro — im Aisha, AE. With me is Mateo, our SE, and Lina from CS. We're going to walk through a playbook for tiered rate fencing and fallback routing across org and project keys.

00:28 Speaker 2 (Jordan): Thanks Aisha. Samir and Priya are on the line too. We're interested because our transaction enrichment pipeline is spiking and we want cost protection but zero impact to latency for premium customers.

00:47 Mateo (SE): Totally. We'll start with keying topologies — org keys map to billing/orgs and project keys for teams/apps. The idea is you can apply quota bands at the org level, then more granular project-level burst allowances.

01:12 Priya (Lead SRE): Quick clarification — when you say "burst allowances" is that token-based or concurrency-based? We need both for batch scoring vs realtime endpoints.

01:30 Mateo: Great question. Redwood supports both. You can set per-project token quotas, plus concurrency caps. We also support leaky-bucket drains so bursts don't "ate up" baseline capacity. Sorry, "ate up" — eat up, yeah.

01:52 Speaker 3 (Samir): We're heavily compliance-driven. For PII, do you recommend Hosted with VPC peering or Private? Our security folks lean Private but that's a big lift.

02:08 Lina (CSM): We see two patterns: most customers start Hosted with VPC egress and strict retention + KMS; then move to Private for regulated flows. We can show a hybrid: host sensitive calls to Private endpoints, non-sensitive calls to Hosted with fallback routing.

02:36 Jordan: Can you show the console for that? How are quotas enforced and visible?

02:45 Mateo: Sure, I'll share screen. (Noise) Alright, so in Console > Quotas you can define policy objects: org-quota, project-quota, burst-window. You can also set routing rules — sticky routing keeps a project pinned to a model variant unless health checks fail, then fallback rules kick in.

03:15 Mateo: [screen nav] Here is an example we prepared: Apollo-org has a base throughput of 500 rps across projects, project A has 200 rps reserved, project B 150, and there is a burst pool of 250 tokens that's first-class. If the main model reaches latency SLOs we can auto-fallback to a quantized cheaper model variant with slightly lower quality.

03:48 Elliot (PM): When fallback happens, is it transparent? Do we get a header or metric so product can instrument quality shift?

04:05 Mateo: Yes — fallbacks are annotated in the response headers and in per-request tracing. Console flags the model variant and a "quality delta" metric if you enable evaluation sets. You can also route a percentage of traffic to fallback via canary rules for A/B testing.

04:33 Priya: Our biggest concern: cost spikes during fraud spikes. We want a hard cap to protect budget, but also want degraded service for non-critical workloads rather than full block. Can Redwood do prioritized degradation?

05:00 Mateo: Yep — you can assign priority lanes. High-priority keys get reserved throughput and guaranteed latency; mid and low get reduced token allotments or are redirected to batch endpoints with lower cost. You can also set "grace windows" so a high-priority request that exceeds base quota can borrow from the burst pool with pre-configured chargebacks.

05:30 Samir: Are chargebacks visible in billing? We need line items by project for reconciliation.

05:44 Aisha: Billing exports include per-org and per-project usage with labels for fallback usage, caching hits, and K-V cache warm percentages. We can provide a sample billing CSV and mapping rules.

06:05 Jordan: Could you walk through a failure scenario — svc region outage and how traffic gets rerouted?

06:20 Mateo: Sure. Smart routing uses region policies: primary region, secondary region, and model-variant fallback. On primary loss, traffic routes to secondary with sticky session fallbacks, or to a cheaper model variant if secondary capacity is limited. We also support circuit breakers to avoid cascading across teams.

06:48 Speaker 2 (Jordan): Any noise around cold KV caches when routing to another region?

07:00 Mateo: There will be a warmup cost — KV cache is per-runtime; Redis-backed prefix cache can be replicated but there is an eventual sync window. We show expected latency delta on the dashboard.

07:24 Priya: About the prefix/KV cache — are those transparent or do we need to change our code to leverage them?

07:33 Mateo: Mostly transparent if you use our SDK and pass the same session ID or conversation ID. For persistent inference in batch jobs you can explicitly warm with the warm API.

07:50 Samir: Can you quantify the cost delta of fallback to quantized model — say our baseline is a 70B FP16 model, fallback is a 13B int8 variant. What do we see?

08:05 Mateo: It varies by sequence length but ballpark 3-4x token cost reduction for int8 smaller model. Latency could be 30-60% lower but quality differences are domain-specific. Optimize gives recommendations based on your eval prompts.

08:30 Elliot: We want to protect customer-facing transactions — they must hit high-quality model. Internal enrichment can use fallback. How granular can we make routing?

08:45 Mateo: Very granular. You can route by project key, endpoint path, or token metadata. For example, transactions.endpoint/charge can be pinned to org-premium key while /enrich uses project dev key.

09:05 Priya: Any real-world examples?

09:12 Mateo: We had a payments customer that reserved dedicated capacity for high-priority routes and used hosted fallback for lower-priority analysis. During a traffic surge they borrowed burst capacity and then automatically scaled down. Billing showed clear line items so finance modeled the peak costs.

09:40 Jordan: Security specifics: we need audit logs per request and proof of deletion. How granular are your audit logs and retention policies?

09:52 Lina: Audit logs are per-request and include model variant, routing decision, and project key. Retention is configurable; we support integration with customer SIEM and S3 export. For deletion, we provide retention TTLs and redact options; for Private we can guarantee no logs leave customer VPC.

10:20 Samir: KMS — we use a cloud HSM. Can we bring our keys?

10:28 Lina: Yes, we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSMs). For Hosted we do envelope encryption with customer CMK; for Private you control the KMS entirely.

10:44 Elliot: Ok demo time — Mateo, show how to create a tiered policy and simulate a spike.

11:00 Mateo: (screen) Creating a new policy: name it "apollo-tier-guard". Add org-level quota, then add project overrides. Set burst pool 20% of org baseline with per-project reservation. Now open the simulator — we can replay a 5k req/min sample and watch quota hits and fallback triggers.

11:28 Mateo: Running simulator... you'll see project B reaches quota, then burst pool absorbs a portion, then low-priority routes are redirected to batch. Fallback to small model variant triggers when avg latency > 300ms.

12:02 Priya: I see traces showing fallback. The trace IDs — are they compatible with our tracing system? We use Jaeger.

12:14 Mateo: We export traces in OTLP format; you can ingest them into Jaeger or Datadog. The Console also has exporters.

12:30 Jordan: How about quantitative evaluation? We have a set of prompts that are sensitive to hallucination. Can we run an A/B using your Optimize evaluator?

12:44 Mateo: Absolutely — Optimize can run prompt sets across model variants and generate quality deltas. We tie regressions to PRs and can alert on quality drift so you don't accidentally shift baseline during a rollout.

13:05 Speaker 4 (Elliot): If we do a pilot, can we have a quota sandbox so devs can test without touching production quotas?

13:15 Aisha: Yes, sandbox projects are standard. You can create a project key scoped to test environments with separate billing and limited burst pools.

13:30 Samir: A couple questions from security: Do you persist raw prompts by default? We need to avoid any raw storage of sensitive tokens.

13:44 Lina: By default Hosted retains prompts for 30 days for debugging, but you can disable retention or enable automatic redaction. For Private, retention is under your control. We also support PII redaction hooks pre-send.

14:05 Jordan: We want to test the budget protections — a hard stop for non-critical projects after spend X. How are hard caps enforced?

14:18 Mateo: You can configure hard caps at org and project level. When hit, we return a 429 with a specific hint (X-RateLimit-Reason). You can also configure graceful degradation that switches low-priority traffic to a cached result or returns a summarized response with cheaper tokens.

14:44 Priya: Is there an API to query remaining budget/quota programmatically?

14:52 Mateo: Yes — quota-status endpoints and SDK methods. You can poll or subscribe to webhook alerts for low-quota warnings and breaches.

15:10 Elliot: On routing policies, is there support for percent-based spillover? e.g., 20% of overflow goes to secondary region and 80% to fallback model?

15:25 Mateo: Yep you can define weighted spillover; rules engine accepts weights, health thresholds, and canaries.

15:40 Jordan: About costs — can you produce an estimated S-curve showing expected monthly cost for different burst profiles?

15:52 Aisha: We'll include a cost model spreadsheet with scenarios and also pre-run a benchmark with your traffic sample to generate an S-curve. Mateo will own the benchmark artifact.

16:10 Samir: How hard is Dedicated? Timeline and minimums?

16:20 Lina: Dedicated typically takes 6-8 weeks to provision from contract signature for standard configs; quicker for pre-canned shapes. Minimum commitments depend on GPU class; we can share standard packages. Private on-prem timelines vary widely.

16:44 Jordan: For the pilot we probably want Hosted with VPC and can we enable early dedicated reservation for high-priority lanes?

16:56 Aisha: Yes that's a common hybrid. You can reserve a small dedicated pool for premium traffic and keep general workloads on Hosted with fallback routing.

17:10 Elliot: A bit of housekeeping — can you send the sample policy JSON we just created?

17:18 Mateo: Will do. I'll export the policy and attach as a gist. (link pasted) https://gist.github.com/redwood/apollo-tier-guard-sample

17:34 Priya: Any latency SLO guarantees on Hosted? If we go hosted, what SLA for p95/p99?

17:46 Lina: Our Hosted SLA covers availability; p95/p99 latency SLOs vary by model and region. We publish performance profiles per model in the catalog. For stricter SLOs, Dedicated is recommended.

18:05 Samir: Competitor question — do you have customers who moved from Orion AI and saw cost savings?

18:16 Aisha: Yes, a couple of infra customers moved and cited better cost predictability and observability as the main win. We'll include references if helpful.

18:30 Jordan: Ok let's talk pilot scope. We want to validate: cost protection during peak, no regression for customer-facing flows, and security posture for PII. Two-week pilot with traffic replay sounds good.

18:46 Aisha: Sounds perfect. Proposed pilot plan: week 0: configuration and policy setup; week 1: traffic replay + benchmarking; week 2: live canary with small percentage of production traffic and evaluation.

19:05 Elliot: How will we measure "no regression"?

19:12 Mateo: We'll run pre-defined eval prompts and measure answer quality and hallucination rates across variants. Also track latency SLOs and error rates. Optimize will produce a digestible scoreboard.

19:30 Priya: Any gotchas for us when creating project keys — naming conventions or limits?

19:38 Mateo: Use structured naming: org.project.env.purpose — helps with billing export and routing rules. There's a soft limit on number of keys per org but we can increase it upon request.

19:55 Jordan: One quick ask — can fallbacks be made to external model endpoints in case Redwood is out of capacity? We have partner models in-house.

20:10 Mateo: Yes, you can add external model providers as endpoints in routing policies. We support proxying calls and applying the same quota logic. There is a small configuration to map response formats.

20:30 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Ok we're nearing time, we'll wrap with confirmations. Lina will send security pack within 48 hours, Mateo will share benchmark config and sample policy, Jordan will upload traffic sample, Aisha will schedule pilot kickoff. Any final Qs?

20:50 Samir: One more — can you show how billing export looks like? Quick peek?

21:00 Aisha: (shares) Here's a sample CSV: columns include date, org_id, project_key, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd, fallback_flag, cache_hit. We will send the template in the follow-up.

21:20 Elliot: Great. Also please add an entry in the ticket tracker for pilot acceptance criteria so we can sign off once metrics are met.

21:34 Aisha: Will do. We'll include acceptance criteria doc with thresholds for latency, quality, and cost.

21:45 Jordan: Thanks all. This was helpful.

21:50 Aisha: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links and next steps.
